candidate.title: Warrant
candidate.problemStatement: Agent action authority is commonly reconstructed from chat, transient approval dialogs, hidden policy, credentials, evidence, and human memory, so downstream participants cannot reliably determine why a bounded action may continue, what exact subject and purpose were authorized, or whether authority has expired, narrowed, or been revoked.
candidate.scope: A provisional purpose-bound, fact-addressed authorization object for bounded continuation. The name, universal contract, relation to existing capability and mandate systems, cross-domain applicability, novelty, and Primitive status remain open.

observationPerspective.bearer: human or agent viewing one permission prompt, task authorization block, credential, or policy result
observationPerspective.proximity: inside one authorization event but outside durable work and evidence lineage
consequences: bears repeated approval, unclear scope, authority drift, revocation, and audit cost

genesis.observation: Separating a persistent Pursuit, contextual Atlas, and experienced Episode from the fused Proof-Carrying Work Object still left one necessary boundary: a durable decision that binds exact subject, purpose, facts, authority, holder, allowed continuation, constraints, and residual risk.
genesis.candidateObject: A Warrant is a purpose-bound, fact-addressed authorization for bounded continuation.
genesis.claimBoundary: This cut records a provisional authorization-object hypothesis. It does not claim that every approval requires a durable Warrant, that Warrant replaces enforcement or assessment, that remote authority is locally valid, or that the candidate is novel, universal, product-ready, or accepted.

transformedPerspective.bearer: downstream participant deciding whether a specific action may continue for a specific purpose
transformedPerspective.role: authority issuer, holder, local acceptor, or later auditor
transformedPerspective.proximity: inside the fact, authority, action, and consequence boundary
consequences: bears unauthorized action, repeated investigation, over-broad delegation, stale authority, and revocation failure

genesis.transformation: The observer moved from one approval interaction to the participant who must later explain and enforce why an exact continuation was legitimate across agents, tools, and organizations.
genesis.newlyVisibleNeed: Authorization must become an independently addressable, purpose-bound fact object rather than remain ambient in chat, credentials, mutable task text, or hidden policy.
genesis.methodNotes: The original fused candidate combined epistemic basis, work identity, execution history, and continuation permission. Structural compression retained the minimum object joining facts and recognized authority to an exact bounded action.

contactSides: authority issuer, policy, evidence producer, or approving participant
agent, tool, downstream gate, operator, or organization deciding whether to continue
boundaryPressure.implicitHandling: Purpose, evidence, scope, issuer authority, holder, constraints, and revocation are reconstructed from prompts, policy engines, credentials, task text, logs, and human memory.

pressureChanges.description: Agents increasingly request, derive, exercise, and inspect authority without sharing one conversational context.
Real-world agent actions require exact limits, recognized issuers, local acceptance, attenuation, expiry, and revocation.
Authorization crosses provider approval systems, operating-system enforcement, organization policy, and domain-specific evidence.
Over-broad or stale authority can change source, publish artifacts, move money, disclose information, or alter real systems.

observedFailures: A downstream participant must reconstruct why an action was permitted.
Mutable task scope silently broadens a prior approval.
Remote or producer-declared authority is mistaken for local permission.
Revocation edits or deletes history instead of preserving an auditable lifecycle.
Successful execution is mistaken for legitimate authorization.
boundaryPressure.mediationClaim: A Warrant may bind exact subject, purpose, basis, authority, holder, action set, constraints, and lifecycle so continuation can be independently inspected and locally accepted.
boundaryPressure.internalObjectAlternative: Existing capability, authorization decision, verifiable credential, mandate, policy, and event-log compositions may provide all required behavior without a new Warrant Primitive.

pressure: Task and approval scope drifting independently
Need for revocable and attenuable cross-agent continuation
Separation between epistemic evidence and operational permission
grounding.evidenceBoundary: Public reconstruction of the authorization split recorded on 2026-07-17. No common implementation, enforcement integration, independent adopter, multi-domain attenuation test, benchmark, or security review is included.
knownGaps: No final name or proven universal minimum closure
No common local and remote acceptance protocol
No implementation of immutable body plus append-only lifecycle events
No measured reduction in repeated approval cost
No adversarial delegation, revocation, expiry, or confused-deputy qualification
No proof that existing capability or mandate standards are insufficient

alternatives.name: Transient approval or provider permission
alternatives.reason: This may be sufficient for one local execution but usually lacks durable purpose, fact basis, cross-agent identity, lineage, and later reassessment.

alternatives.name: Capability token
alternatives.reason: Capabilities strongly represent exercisable authority but may not preserve the purpose-bound epistemic basis, residual risk, and independent judgment expected here.

alternatives.name: Verifiable credential or authorization credential
alternatives.reason: Credentials may carry signed claims and authority but may not define the full continuation lifecycle or local purpose-bound acceptance.

alternatives.name: Mandate, permit, policy decision, or access-control record
alternatives.reason: One of these existing domain objects may already be the correct boundary, with Warrant only a naming profile.

alternatives.name: Passport or proof-carrying artifact
alternatives.reason: A passport may justify trust in a result but does not necessarily authorize a holder to take the next action.

alternatives.name: No new Primitive
alternatives.reason: The candidate may be a composition profile across evidence, policy, capability, credential, and lifecycle event standards.

contractModel.identity: An immutable warrant_ref for one purpose-bound authorization decision, with exact subject revision, issuer, holder, and lineage.
contractModel.boundary: Exact subject and revision root, purpose, issuer and recognized authority, holder, allowed and forbidden actions, fact and evidence basis, constraints, expiry, delegation and attenuation rules, residual risk, and lifecycle references.
contractModel.authority: The issuer must possess recognized authority for the bounded continuation; the recipient or local policy independently decides whether to accept an imported Warrant. A Warrant explains authorization but does not replace operating-system, sandbox, provider, or domain enforcement.
contractModel.lifecycle: requested -> issued, conditionally issued, or denied -> accepted or rejected locally -> exercised -> expired, revoked, exhausted, or superseded

minimumClosure.notes: Exact subject, purpose, basis, authority, holder, action set, constraints, and lifecycle appear load-bearing, but no common implementation has tested whether all fields are minimal.

deletion.notes: Without Warrant, authority remains ambient or reconstructed, but an existing capability, mandate, or policy-decision composition may already remove that burden.

fuse.notes: Approvals, mandates, capabilities, credentials, and policy decisions appear structurally related, but shared operations and security semantics have not survived cross-domain implementation.

falsifiers: Existing capability, credential, mandate, or policy systems provide the full contract without repeated reconstruction.
Fact-addressed authorization does not reduce clarification, approval, or audit cost.
Purpose-bound evidence cannot be safely interpreted across local policy boundaries.
Attenuation, delegation, expiry, and revocation cannot be made safe and comprehensible.
The Warrant becomes an ambient permission, hidden routing mechanism, or self-certification path.
The object adds bureaucracy while enforcement systems still require unrelated approvals.
A common contract erases necessary domain-specific authority distinctions.

dogfood.notes: Embedded standing authorization and release/continuation examples motivate the candidate, but this public cut contains no common Warrant runtime or independent security qualification.

decision.reason: Separating persistent work identity, contextual facts, and execution history leaves a coherent fact-to-action authorization object, but minimum closure, relation to existing standards, security, transfer, deletion, fuse, and dogfood evidence remain unresolved.
residualRisks: The candidate may rename an existing capability or mandate composition.
The legal and epistemic meanings of Warrant may create false assurance.
A machine-readable Warrant may be mistaken for enforcement or universal validity.
Multi-Pursuit or dynamic subject selectors may silently expand authority.
First-party workflow may overfit software and release governance.
Authorization convenience may outrun security review.
